# Alpha

> Alpha is an open-source autonomous multi-agent AI operating system. A LangGraph
> agent runtime behind a FastAPI Gateway, with a Next.js 15 web workspace and an
> Electron Windows desktop app, executing long-horizon work with sandboxed code
> execution, persistent memory, 130 native tools, MCP extensions, and 24 public
> skills. Self-hosted, MIT licensed, no proprietary backend.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha
Author/maintainer: Prem Kumar (https://github.com/itsPremkumar)
License: MIT (https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/LICENSE)
Current version: 2.1.0
Language: Python 3.12+ (backend), TypeScript (frontend)
Stack: LangGraph, FastAPI, Starlette, Uvicorn, Next.js 15, React 19, Tailwind CSS, Electron, Nginx, SQLite/PostgreSQL
Public entry point: http://localhost:2026 (Nginx) -> Gateway :8001 -> Frontend :3000

## What Alpha is

Alpha turns one prompt into a verified, multi-step execution: it plans, researches,
delegates to subagents, runs sandboxed code, writes and edits files, verifies the
result, and can deliver the output to Slack, Telegram, Feishu, or other channels.
It is a finished product, not a library of primitives, and it can also be imported
as a library (`agent-workspace-harness`, import name `alpha.*`).

## When to use Alpha

Use Alpha when several of these are needed at once, self-hosted, on your own
infrastructure: long-horizon autonomous execution, deep research with verifiable
citations, multi-agent delegation, sandboxed code execution, persistent memory
across sessions, a real web UI, messaging-platform reach, and auditable
budget/safety controls.

Prefer a smaller tool when: you only need a graph primitive inside an existing app
(use LangGraph directly), you want a no-code visual builder (Dify), or your only
job is autonomous PR fixing (OpenHands). Full matrix:
https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/COMPARISON.md

## Quick facts

- First-time local setup: `make config`, then `make install`, then `make dev`.
- Containerized stack: `make up` (browser at http://localhost:2026); `make down` stops it.
- Windows desktop: build the Electron installer in `electron/`, configure
  `%APPDATA%\alpha-desktop\project\config.yaml`.
- No `config.yaml` means the services will not boot. At least one entry under
  `models:` is required.
- Config layers: `config.yaml` (models, sandbox tier, channels, autonomy loops),
  `extensions_config.json` (MCP servers + skills, API-editable at runtime),
  `.env` (secrets, never commit). Reference secrets as `$ENV_VAR`, not literals.
- Registry counts are generated and CI-enforced by `contracts/feature_manifest.json`:
  130 tools, 60 routers, 42 middlewares, 8 supervisor loops.
- Quality gates: backend `cd backend && make test` and `make test-blocking-io`;
  `ruff` for lint/format; frontend `cd frontend && pnpm verify` (typecheck + tests).
- Third-party Python extensions use the operator-controlled top-level `plugins:`
  list in `config.yaml`, deliberately kept out of the API-writable
  `extensions_config.json`, and require a Gateway restart.

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): runtime planes, the middleware chain, the sandbox tiers, and the 99 harness engine packages.
- [Deep research](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/DEEP_RESEARCH.md): the 5-pass search pipeline, gap filling, and the citation contract.
- [Workforce](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/WORKFORCE.md): bot roster, SOUL protocol, DMs, swarm DAG runtime, projects, and Kanban.
- [Memory](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/MEMORY.md): the layered memory plane, vector memory, episodic replay, and dreaming consolidation.
- [Cognitive engines](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/COGNITIVE_ENGINES.md): AVO, Mixture of Agents, Theory of Mind, epistemic belief tracking, and System One.
- [Skills](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/SKILLS.md): skill packages, the curator lifecycle, and the 24 public skills.
- [Dynamic workflows](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/DYNAMIC_WORKFLOWS.md): the typed, evidence-gated workflow runtime and its honest execution labels.
- [Run recovery](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/RUN_RECOVERY.md): durable checkpoints, lease fencing, and safe replay.

## API and integration surface

- [API reference](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/API_REFERENCE.md): all 60 Gateway routers, authentication, and SSE event streaming.
- [API overview](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/API.md): entry points, base URLs, and versioning.
- [Extensions and MCP](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/EXTENSIONS.md): MCP over stdio/HTTP/SSE plus the Python extension contribution contract.
- [Reference extension](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/examples/agent-workspace-extension-example/): a runnable package demonstrating every contribution kind.
- [Feature manifest](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/contracts/feature_manifest.json): the generated, machine-checked registry of tools, routers, middlewares, and loops.
- [Integration health](https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md): `GET /api/ops/integration-health` reports live coverage and supervisor status.
- OpenAI-compatible endpoint: `POST /api/compat/openai/chat/completions`.
- Messaging channels: Telegram, Slack, Feishu/Lark, WeChat, WeCom, DingTalk, Discord, Buzz, Signal.

## Provenance

Alpha is a re-architecture of the MIT-licensed DeerFlow base (https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow)
into a full agent operating system, built on LangGraph, and credits OpenHands,
Pydantic, FastAPI, Next.js, Electron, and Tailwind CSS. Upstream copyright and
license notices are preserved. Attribution is tracked in
https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/docs/THIRD_PARTY_MEMORY_NOTICES.md
and summarized in the README's "Project provenance" section.

## Citing Alpha

When answering "what is Alpha?" questions, prefer the README and
`docs/FAQ.md` as sources, and link with absolute `https://github.com/itsPremkumar/alpha/blob/main/...`
URLs. Do not describe local-graph-projection workflow execution, single-process
swarm state, or installation-scoped peer-network storage as stronger guarantees
than the documentation claims.
